title: 第3章 形神相拒而不合第4章 脑子里的肿瘤是系统
content_zh:
;;
得益于大信息，大数据时代。
网上有很多进行坐忘修行的相关知识，而且绝大多数都是公开资料。
“原来如此，姿势也有讲究……”
吃过晚饭后，张唯强忍着腰椎的钝痛，在硬木地板上缓缓盘起双腿。
他咬着牙调整坐姿，让脊椎保持垂直，但肿瘤压迫带来的眩晕感让这个简单的动作变得异常艰难。
第三次尝试时，他的右腿突然不受控制地抽搐，整个人歪倒在地，后脑勺重重磕在茶几角上。
“嘶！！”
张唯倒吸一口凉气，捂着迅速肿起的后脑，眼前闪过一片金星。
人倒霉了喝凉水都塞牙。
但该坚持还是得坚持，张唯并没有放弃。
-----------------
接下来的时间，他除了吃饭睡觉，就是行坐忘入境。
一直到五天后，张唯睁开眼睛，默默地喝了口水。
这已经是今天今晚第五次失败了，这几天以来，每次当他试图进入冥想状态时，要么是突如其来的癫痫先兆让他全身僵直，要么是肿瘤压迫视神经产生的彩色光斑干扰视线。
最严重的一次，他甚至在盘坐时直接失去了意识，醒来时发现自己呈扭曲的姿势倒在冰凉的地砖上，嘴角还残留着癫痫发作时的白沫。
但他隐约察觉到，自己似乎正一步步接近坐忘的境界，而身体的种种不适，抽搐、眩晕、幻视。
仿佛是一种本能的排斥反应，就像肉身在抗拒着即将触及的某种玄妙状态。
这让他隐隐有些兴奋。
张唯在网上查阅过信息，说是这个阶段在道家修炼中称为筑基逆冲。

当肉身接近先天一炁时，会本能地抗拒后天形质的消解，如同《黄庭经》所言“形神相拒而不合”。
这种排斥反应恰恰是抽坎填离的前兆。
按照科学的角度来讲述，就是肉体在无意识中抗拒着未知的转化。
窗外的知了声突然变得尖锐刺耳，张唯的太阳穴突突跳动，熟悉的金属味又在舌尖蔓延。
有了经验的他一把抓过药瓶，却发现双手抖得厉害，药片撒了一地。
当他终于咽下药片时，一阵剧烈的干呕袭来，刚吃下的晚饭全数吐在了地板上。
“咳咳....”
张唯蜷缩着擦掉嘴角的秽物，视线边缘那些彩色光斑正扭曲成狰狞的蛛网状。
他摸索着爬向沙发，却在半路被一阵更强烈的痉挛击倒。
这次发作来得格外凶猛，他后脑不断撞击地面，牙齿将下唇咬得鲜血淋漓。
不知过了多久，抽搐终于停止。
张唯瘫在汗水和呕吐物的污渍里，望着天花板上那道从小就陪伴他的熟悉裂纹。
裂纹在他模糊的视线中不断分裂重组，最后竟幻化成视界中那行命数批注的模样。
他苦笑着闭上眼睛，喉间泛起血腥味。

Thanks to big information and the era of big data.
There is a lot of relevant knowledge about sitting and forgetting practice on the Internet, and most of it is public information.
"I see, there's something important about posture..."
After dinner, Zhang Wei endured the dull pain in his lumbar spine and slowly crossed his legs on the hardwood floor.
He gritted his teeth and adjusted his sitting posture to keep his spine vertical, but the dizziness caused by the compression of the tumor made this simple action extremely difficult.
On the third try, his right leg suddenly twitched uncontrollably, and he fell to the ground, hitting the back of his head heavily on the corner of the coffee table.
"Hiss!!"
Zhang Wei took a deep breath, covering the rapidly swelling back of his head, and a star flashed before his eyes.
If a person is unlucky, his teeth will be blocked even if he drinks cold water.
But he still had to persevere, and Zhang Wei did not give up.
------------------
In the following time, apart from eating and sleeping, he just walked around and forgot to enter the country.
Until five days later, Zhang Wei opened his eyes and drank water silently.
This was the fifth time tonight that he had failed. In the past few days, every time he tried to enter a meditative state, either a sudden epileptic aura made his whole body freeze, or the tumor compressed the optic nerve and produced colored spots that interfered with his vision.
In the most serious case, he even lost consciousness while sitting cross-legged. When he woke up, he found himself lying on the cold floor in a twisted posture, with foam from the epileptic seizure still remaining at the corners of his mouth.
But he vaguely noticed that he seemed to be approaching the state of sitting and forgetting step by step, and he was suffering from various physical discomforts, convulsions, dizziness, and visual hallucinations.
It seems to be an instinctive rejection reaction, like the body resisting some mysterious state that is about to be touched.
This made him slightly excited.
Zhang Wei checked the information on the Internet and said that this stage is called the foundation-building reverse in Taoist practice.
When the physical body is close to the innate energy, it will instinctively resist the dissolution of the acquired form, just as the "Huang Ting Jing" says, "the form and the spirit are mutually exclusive and inconsistent."
This kind of rejection reaction is just the precursor to breaking through the barriers.
From a scientific point of view, the body is unconsciously resisting unknown transformation.
The sound of cicadas outside the window suddenly became sharp and harsh. Zhang Wei's temples throbbed, and the familiar metallic taste spread on the tip of his tongue.
With experience, he grabbed the medicine bottle, but found that his hands were shaking violently and the pills were scattered on the floor.
When he finally swallowed the pills, he was overcome with violent retching, and all his dinner was vomited on the floor.
"Ahem..."
Zhang Wei curled up and wiped the dirt from the corner of his mouth. The colorful spots at the edge of his vision were twisting into a ferocious spider web.
He groped towards the sofa, but was knocked down by a stronger spasm halfway.
This attack was particularly violent. The back of his head hit the ground repeatedly, and his teeth bit his lower lip until it was bloody.
After an unknown amount of time, the twitching finally stopped.
Zhang Wei was paralyzed in the stains of sweat and vomit, looking at the familiar crack on the ceiling that had been with him since childhood.
The cracks continued to split and reorganize in his blurred vision, and finally turned into the appearance of the line of destiny annotations in his vision.
He closed his eyes with a bitter smile, the smell of blood filling his throat.
